children: New Delhi, Nov. 2 -- Reliance Industries share price surged as much as 5.91% in Monday's trading session after the Mukesh Ambani-led oil-to-telecom conglomerate reported strong set of numbers during the July-September quarter FY27.
RIL stock opened at Rs.1,228.10 apiece on NSE today, as compared to previous close of Rs.1,164.90 last week on Friday and touched an intraday high of Rs.1,237.30 on 2 November.

Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) reported a 33.8% year-on-year (YoY) growth in consolidated profit after tax (PAT), including its share of associates and joint ventures, at Rs.29,550 crore for Q2FY27, compared with Rs.22,092 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Net profit attributable to the company's shareholders increased 40% YoY to Rs.25,548 crore.

The company's consolidated revenue rose 27.8% YoY to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore. The latest quarterly profit also surpassed the Rs.23,196 crore recorded in the previous quarter, marking a fresh high for India's largest listed company by market capitalisation.

The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) segment was the biggest contributor to earnings growth, supported by stronger global transportation fuel cracks and an improvement in petrochemical margins. The segment's EBITDA surged 67.9% YoY to Rs.25,203 crore, while revenue climbed 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore.

Global supply disruptions arising from the West Asia conflict, including tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, as well as attacks on refining infrastructure across the region and Russia, drove fuel cracks to 3-3.7 times their year-ago levels. Meanwhile, the average price of Dated Brent crude stood at $97 per barrel during the quarter, registering a 40.6% YoY increase.

The improvement in refining margins came despite geopolitical uncertainties, higher crude premiums and elevated freight costs. Reliance said its diversified crude procurement strategy and flexibility in optimising product placement helped it capitalise on favourable market conditions. The company also achieved its highest-ever crude processing volumes by increasing supplies from the Americas and the Mediterranean and redirecting exports towards markets offering better net realisations.
